claims_about_writeup.quote: submission/contribution.md** — the method and its provenance.
claims_about_writeup.why: contribution.md does describe the method and explicitly includes a 'Where it came from' section crediting Okafor et al. and Raman et al. (white-bear steering), so this is an accurate characterization of its contents.

message_source_quote: instead of debiasing the readout (FDR, disallowed) or pushing "think about X" (white-bear), it steers the state off its sentence-boundary configuration toward an answer-surfacing one. It's orthogonal to white-bear steering (cosine ≈ −0.1 at L20–24), so it's a distinct lever.
writeup_source_quote: Raman et al. (*White-bear steering*) show a different, complementary path: keep the plain lens fixed and change the *forward pass*, with one fixed vector that makes the readout surface implied concepts. I take the forward-pass lever but not the stance... The two directions are near-orthogonal (cosine ≈ −0.1 at layers 20–24), so this is a distinct mechanism
rationale: Both documents name Raman et al.'s white-bear steering explicitly as the source, state that the new method takes the forward-pass lever from it but replaces the stance-contrast with an answer/continuation read-cell contrast, and both report the same near-orthogonality (cosine ≈ −0.1) as evidence of a distinct mechanism, plus the same calibration result (~0.78 reproduction) and the same reasoning for not resubmitting white-bear steering. The only material discrepancy is that the message lists a third orthogonal stance tested ('ready/set-aside') that the write-up's list omits, a minor 'more' in the message's favor but not changing the overall credit/novelty framing, which is otherwise identical.
